logline: A wheelchair-bound K-pop fan time-travels to her idol's high-school years and races to prevent his death while untangling the consequences of rewriting the past.

renewal.note: No Season 2 announced; tvN has not renewed the series as of June 2026. K-drama limited runs rarely continue.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.5 and a MyDramaList score in the 9.1-9.2 range reflect genuine cross-border fandom; the time-travel mechanics frustrate some critics but the lead chemistry and emotional pacing drive an unusually high completion rate.

seasons.review_body: Lovely Runner landed as a breakout K-drama of the first half of 2024, turning Byeon Woo-seok into a major regional hit and elevating Kim Hye-yoon as one of the standout contenders. The time-travel scaffold is familiar, but the series runs it with enough emotional precision and comic lightness to keep plot-logic stretches from derailing momentum. Viewership and discussion repeatedly point to lead chemistry, along with the show’s ability to make its stakes feel genuinely personal despite the genre machinery. Western trade coverage was limited, with momentum largely sustained by stronger fan-driven conversation. The back half tests some viewers with pacing slack and time-loop repetition, while the prevailing read is that the emotional payoff still lands.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Lovely Runner Season 1 Episode 1 aired April 8, 2024 on tvN with simultaneous Netflix availability as the premiere of the drama that turned Byeon Woo-seok into a major regional star. The series earned an IMDb score of 8.5 and a MyDramaList score in the 9.1 range from substantial audience bases, reflecting a breakout K-drama of the first half of 2024. The premiere's outrageous premise - Im Sol, a wheelchair-bound K-pop fan, time-travels to 2008 and finds herself standing next to her idol Ryu Sun-jae as a teenager - is executed with warmth and speed that prevent the genre machinery from overwhelming the character work. Byeon Woo-seok's performance in the first episode signals immediately that the show has something real underneath its fantasy structure: a teenage idol who does not know he is being saved, performing natural adolescent charisma rather than celebrity knowledge. Kim Hye-yoon's Im Sol makes her decision to stay in 2008 in a single wordless beat - the series' thesis delivered without explanation - and the premiere's completion rate across both platforms reflected an audience that found the implicit promise worth following.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Im Sol, a wheelchair-bound K-pop fan, time-travels to 2008 and finds herself standing next to her idol Ryu Sun-jae as a teenager. The premise is outrageous; the execution is warm and fast-moving, and Byeon Woo-seok's performance as a teenage idol who doesn't know he's being saved signals immediately that the show has something real underneath its fantasy machinery.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Im Sol realising she is standing in the past and making the decision to stay - the show's thesis delivered in a single wordless beat.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 7
episode_reviews.review_body: Lovely Runner Season 1 Episode 7 aired April 29, 2024 on tvN as the midpoint episode where the show's tonal gear shift from warm comedy to anxious consequence becomes complete. The IMDb series score of 8.5 reflects an audience that found the time-travel mechanics credible enough to generate genuine dread when they start working against Im Sol, and Episode 7 is the episode where this shift is most legible: every change she has made has created new dangers she could not anticipate, and the consequences begin arriving faster than she can redirect them. Byeon Woo-seok and Kim Hye-yoon's lead chemistry, which the first six episodes deployed as comic energy, is carrying real emotional weight by the midpoint - the audience has spent enough time with both characters to find the stakes personal. The MyDramaList score in the 9.1 range reflects an audience that found this gear shift not a structural problem but the show's core achievement: using the time-travel scaffold to generate the kind of dramatic irony that makes the audience want both to warn a character and to watch them figure it out independently.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The midpoint sharpens the time-travel paradox - every change Im Sol makes creates new dangers she couldn't anticipate. The show shifts gear from comedy to something more anxious, and the leads' chemistry is carrying real emotional weight by now rather than just comic energy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A change in the timeline that Im Sol thought would fix things visibly making them worse - the episode that turned the fandom from delighted to devastated.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 13
episode_reviews.review_body: Lovely Runner Season 1 Episode 13 aired May 20, 2024 on tvN as the episode where the show’s structural approach to dramatic irony reaches its pivot: Ryu Sun-jae begins assembling the picture of what Im Sol has been doing across the timeline, and the emotional register shifts from dramatic irony to the more exposed territory of mutual recognition. The IMDb series score of 8.5 and MyDramaList score in the 9.1 range together reflect an audience that found the time-travel premise’s accumulation rewarding rather than repetitive; Episode 13 is where the patience required by the back half’s loop repetition - the acknowledged structural cost of the premise - begins to convert into the emotional payoff those scores reflect. Byeon Woo-seok’s performance as Sun-jae piecing together Im Sol’s behaviour across the timeline is the episode’s central performance challenge: the character understanding something for the first time that the audience has known from the premiere, without the reveal feeling retrospectively obvious. The look on his face when the picture becomes clear is the series’ most-cited individual moment in the back half.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Sun-jae begins to understand what Im Sol has been doing and why, and the show shifts the emotional register from dramatic irony to mutual recognition. The back half’s time-loop repetition is felt most clearly in this episode, where it underscores the growing patience.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sun-jae putting together Im Sol's behaviour across the timeline and the look on his face when the picture becomes clear.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.review_body: Lovely Runner Season 1 Episode 16 aired May 28, 2024 on tvN as the series finale and the episode that explains why the MyDramaList score stayed above 9.1 across a substantial audience. The temporal loop that has driven the season is resolved with emotional precision rather than mechanical plot logic - a choice that prioritises what the time-travel premise is actually about (Im Sol's love and determination to protect someone she cannot lose) over a technically satisfying narrative closure. Byeon Woo-seok and Kim Hye-yoon's chemistry, operational from the premiere, reaches the register in the finale that the MyDramaList score reflects: an audience that found the emotional payoff proportionate to sixteen episodes of investment. PureWow cited the show's 'chemistry and emotional pacing' as the reasons for its unusually high completion rate across streaming platforms. The final scene across time is the series' central promise paid in full - simultaneously predictable in outcome and genuinely moving in execution, which is the specific achievement the 9.1 MyDramaList score and the 8.5 IMDb score together document.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves the temporal loop with emotional precision rather than mechanical plot logic, which is why the MyDramaList score stayed above 9.1. PureWow noted the show's chemistry and emotional pacing as the reasons for its unusually high completion rate, and the finale is the culmination of both.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final scene across time - the show paying off its central promise in a way that is simultaneously predictable and genuinely moving.
